chunks.text: after finishing. Attention shall be given to the curing of concrete containing cement replacement material. The Contractor shall prepare and submit a detailed method statement for curing of concrete and maintaining the curing regime to the standards and times specified. Curing shall be continued for a period of not less than 7 days from the time of placing the concrete. Concrete containing Ground Granulated Blast furnace Slag, Fly Ash or Silica Fume shall be protected for a period of at least 10 days. The concrete shall be kept protected against loss of moisture, rapid temperature change, rain and flowing water, mechanical injury, contamination by airborne dust and sand, drying winds and surface heating by the sun’s rays. The Contractor’s attention is particularly drawn to the importance of starting to cure as early as possible after placing concrete and maintaining full curing procedures throughout, as specified and directed. 126 of 738 67 Any concrete which exhibits plastic settlement or plastic or drying shrinkage cracking or which has not been properly cured is liable to rejection and shall be cut out and replaced with satisfactory concrete by the Contractor at his own expense. The maximum crack width is limited to a value of 0.30 and 0.1 to below table: Table 3-14: Concrete Crack Width Class Designation Description of Environment Design Crack width (mm) XS1 All structural elements except water retaining structure 0.30 XS2 Water retaining structure 0.10 3.1.24.1 Curing Methods All methods to be used for curing and protection of freshly placed concrete must receive the prior approval. These methods shall include the use of curing membranes, water, covers, shades and any other precautions that are required for the Contractor to ensure satisfactory curing of the concrete. The Contractor’s attention is drawn to the recommendations of the American Concrete Institute Standard ACI 308R-01 Guide to Curing Concrete and CIRIA /Concrete Society Guide to the construction of reinforced concrete in the Arabian Peninsula. For large concrete pours, in particular, the avoidance of thermal shock caused by rapid cooling is very important and the external faces of the hardening concrete shall be insulated to prevent heat loss such that the temperature difference specified in this specification is not exceeded. 3.1.24.2 Water Curing Water curing is the preferred method. Where used, the concrete shall be covered with sacking, hessian, or other absorbent material, or a 75 mm layer of sand, kept constantly wet for the minimum curing period, also covered with plastic sheeting to reduce loss by evaporation. Water for curing shall ensure that the temperature of all water used at all stages of the curing process is as close as possible to that of the concrete being cured. 3.1.24.3 Curing Membranes The Contractor shall submit full details of the materials he proposes to use including their comparative efficiency with respect to the specified method of water curing. The efficiency shall be a minimum of 90%. Curing membranes shall be of the resin based white reflective film type which fully degrades by exposure to UV

Reinforcement shall be bent by gradual and uniform application of pressure by suitable machines to the forms and dimensions shown on the Contractor's schedules and in accordance with BS 8666. 3.1.25.8 Fixing of Reinforcement The Contractor shall be responsible for maintaining the reinforcement in the correct position during concreting and to this end reinforcing bars shall be fixed together as shown on the Drawings with such laps as are indicated, all to form a rigid cage. Bar crossings shall be secured with at least one turn of tying wire of minimum gauge 16 (dia 1.29mm), the ends of the tie being twisted together and turned down into the work. Every bar shall be secured in at least two places and in addition tie wire spacing shall be not greater than every fourth intersection. Patent stainless steel ties may be used for securing bars. Spacer units fixed to the reinforcement shall be used in all reinforced concrete to give the cover specified herein, on the Drawings or as directed. In slabs, spacers shall be used to support the bottom face reinforcement and chairs shall be used to support the top face reinforcement. The spacing of spacers and chairs shall be in accordance with ACI 315R-18/BS 7973-2. No ferrous metal part of any device used for connecting bars or for maintaining reinforcement in the correct position shall remain within the specified minimum concrete cover to the reinforcement except where expressly instructed or provided for within the Contract. 129 of 738 70 No permanent spacers to reinforcement shall be allowed to affect the overall uniformity of the surface appearance of Classes F2, F3, F3P, U1B, U2, U3 and U4 surface finishes which shall, in any event, comply with the Specification requirements. Reinforcement temporarily projecting from the concrete at construction or other joints shall be adequately supported and shall not be bent out of position unless expressly permitted or directed. Temporary supports to the reinforcement, other than the mild steel chairs referred to above, shall not be incorporated within the finished concrete. 3.1.25.9 Spacers Spacers shall conform to ACI 315R-18/BS 7973 Parts 1 & 2, shall be as small as practicable for their purpose and shall be securely fixed in place by approved means to ensure that they will not be displaced during the placing, vibration or finishing of the concrete. Favorable consideration will be given to the use of proprietary plastic or precast concrete spacers provided these are suitable for the particular use required. Any precast spacer blocks approved for use shall be at least equal in strength to the body of the concrete in which they are being placed. They shall be of equal durability and where used on an exposed face shall provide a good color match as required under the preceding Clause. Any blocks cast on site will be required to be of the same mix to the main body of the concrete. The use of spacer blocks

▪ All floor drains shall be supplied and installed at the locations and to the details shown on the drawings and as specified herein. ▪ Each floor drain shall be of heavy duty uPVC with "S" or "P" trap complete with chrome plated heavy duty, 200 x 200mm, bronze strainer. The strainer shall be screwed to the body of the drain. All floor drains shall have chrome plated removable covers to their strainers or heavy duty aluminium cover. 4.3.4.10 Clean Outs ▪ All clean outs shall be supplied and installed at the locations and to the details shown on the Drawings and wherever specified herein. ▪ Each clean out shall be of the same material and dimensions as the pipe to be cleaned, and shall be placed in walls, slabs or floors as required for ease of operation. ▪ Where cleanouts terminate in floors, a bronze cleanout tile 200 x 200mm, with screwed and sealed cover shall be provided. Tile and cover shall be chrome plated. 4.3.4.11 Vent Caps ▪ Vent caps shall be supplied and installed on all waste, soil and vent stacks at the locations and to the details shown on the drawings and in accordance with this specification. ▪ Each vent cap shall be of uPVC and shall be solvent cemented onto the waste, vent and soil stack. 4.3.4.12 Septic Tank ▪ This shall be a rectangular chamber of concrete built underground and to dimension and depth as shown on the drawings. ▪ The base, walls and roof shall be of reinforced concrete construction. Concrete shall be to grade C40. ▪ The base shall be constructed on layer of 100mm blinding. For specification relating to concrete, refer to Specification for Concrete Works. ▪ One aluminium ladder shall be provided to access inside each section of the tank for cleaning purposes from time to time. A 600mm x 600mm manhole opening shall be provided on the roof of the septic tank. Adequate manhole cover of minimum size 680mm x 680mm with handgrip shall be provided as described for soak ways. The floor of the tank shall slope 1 in 30 towards one side or centre to facilitate cleaning of sludge and the manhole shall be located directly over this ▪ Initially the septic tank shall be filled with water to its outlet level before sewage is allowed to enter the tank. A small quantity of decaying organic matter should preferably be put into the septic tank to start the initial reaction. 4.3.4.13 Contaminated Water Drainage ▪ The Contaminated Water drainage system is required to collect specific discharges of predominantly contaminated water together with floor spillages within the buildings and other contaminant spillages. Flow rates, salinity, other contaminant levels and temperatures of the contaminated drainage shall be determined. ▪ Sources of possible spillage are to be routed via tundishes and hard piped systems above- ground as detailed by the CONTRACTOR'S piping/mechanical department, discharging to suitable lined reinforced concrete gullies and trenches from where the contaminated material shall be routed

Appendix D presents the Engineered Fill requirements. 8.5 Suitable and Unsuitable Material Based on laboratory tests the investigated soils are classified as A-1-a, A-1-b, A-2-4(0), A-2-6, A-2-7, A-7-6, A-4, A-6 material as per AASHTO classification. These materials classified as A-1-a, A-1-b and A-2-4 are suitable for reuse as fill around footings or for general fill. This could indicate a fractured rock but also could indicate the presence of some cavities. Therefore, the condition of rock should be evaluated after excavation and during foundation inspection visit to provide the proper recommendation. 8.7 Corrosion Control According to the chemical analysis which has been conducted on the subsurface soil, it is recommended to use a Portland sulphate resisting type of cement (Type V SRC) in the foundation and subsurface construction. Cement content should not be less than 350kg/m3, while the minimum concrete cover for the reinforcement should not be less than 60mm. with a water/cement ratio not exceeding 0.45. In addition, double coats of bituminous paints should be applied on concrete surface. 8.8 General Sewage System Since there is no sewage system near the project, therefore proper sewage system and tanks for the waste water should be constructed. 9) PREPARATION OF SUITABLE SUBGRADE MATERIAL AND PAVEMENT DESIGN (Reference to M.O.T. Specification) 9.1 Touch Grade Section In the touch grade section, the top twenty (20) centimeters subgrade layer shall be scarified, brought to uniform moisture content within the specified range, and compacted to ninety five percent (95%) of maximum dry density to get a minimum CBR value of 25. The material could be compacted to 98% or even 100% of maximum dry density to get a minimum CBR value of 25 under the approval of the engineer. 9.2 Cut Section In the cut section the bottom twenty (20) centimeters of the subgrade layer shall be scarified, brought to

uniform moisture content within the specified range and compacted to ninety five percent (95%) to get a minimum CBR value of 25. The material could be compacted to 98% or even 100% of maximum dry density to get a minimum CBR value of 25 under the approval of the engineer. 9.3 Fill Material Section (Embankment) At least twenty (20) cm of material placed on the embankment to form the sub-grade layer shall meet the requirement of class A-1-a, A-1-b or A-2-4(0) as determined by MRDTM 210, with a minimum soaked CBR value of twenty five (25) as determined by MRDTM 213 when compacted to ninety five percent (95%) of maximum dry density to get a minimum CBR value of 25. The material could be compacted to 98% or even 100% of maximum dry density to get a minimum CBR value of 25 under 21 of 546 -----------------------------------19------------------------------------- RSM 15492-Rev0 Diriyah Gate Development Project the approval of the engineer. The entire subgrade layer shall be compacted to the specified density in one layer or two approximately equal layers. The pavement design after preparation of the suitable subgrade materials in accordance with section 10.0 is recommended to be as follows: Bituminous Wearing course 05cm Subgrade Material 20cm 10) LIMITATION OF REPORT The recommendations which are given in this report are based on the assumption that the soil condition does not deviate appreciably from those disclosed in the borings and laboratory test results. At the time of construction, if there will be any unanticipated variations in the subsurface conditions or if the proposed construction will differ from those planned at this time, as it is described in this report, the SAFCO should be notified to verify the bottom of excavation so that supplementary recommendations can be given. Please note that all the samples recovered from this investigation will be discarded after 15 days upon the submission of this final report if the client does not ask formally for the retention of the samples. Our company, after having been chosen to perform this geotechnical investigation, shall in case of counter claims be liable only to the extent of what has been paid for the work done. 22 of 546 APPENDIX A SITE & BOREHOLES LOCATION PLANS 23 of 546 24 of 546 2735000.000 2735000.000 2737500.000 2737500.000 658000.000 658000.000 660000.000 660000.000 662000.000 662000.000 N PROJECT NAME: Diriyah Gate Development Project PROJECT REF:RSM 15492 LOCATION: Diriyah, Riyadh, KSA Trail pits Boreholes Legend 25 of 546 APPENDIX B SUMMARY OF FIELD WORK 26 of 546 ---------------------------------------1--------------------------------------- RSM 15492-Rev0 Diriyah Gate Development Project Summary of Field Works Borehole No. Northing (m) Easting (m) Elevation WGS (m) Actual Depth (m) In-Situ Tests Remark BH-1 2737363.120 658331.01 660.038 15 BH-2 2737231.440 658534 657.732 20 Piezometer BH-3R 2737241 658789 656.745 15 Repeated BH-4R 2737165 658941 654.43 15 Repeated BH-7R 2737392 660926 662.165 15 Repeated BH-8 2737276.090 660736.640 660.16 15 BH-9R 2737230 660893 661.799 25 Piezometer & Packer Repeated BH-10 2737092.800 660728.220 662.341 15 BH-12R 2737053 658917 657.92 25 Repeated BH-13 2737010.190
